cards.q: What is IntServ and why does it not scale to large networks?
cards.a: IntServ delivers per-flow, hard QoS guarantees using RSVP to reserve bandwidth end-to-end before traffic flows. Every router holds per-flow state, which is why it does not scale to large networks.

cards.q: What are the key elements of the IntServ model?
cards.a: A flow (per session/application), RSVP reservations (PATH/RESV messages), per-flow reservation state on every router, hard guarantees, and poor scale.

cards.q: What is the role of PATH and RESV messages in RSVP?
cards.a: PATH goes sender to receiver to announce requirements; RESV goes receiver to sender to reserve resources. Each hop runs admission control to accept or reject the reservation.

cards.q: What are the three IntServ service types and what does each guarantee?
cards.a: Guaranteed (hard bandwidth plus delay), Controlled load (QoS under load), and Best effort (no guarantee). Guaranteed is the classic hard-commit service.

cards.q: What commands configure RSVP on an interface and what do they do?
cards.a: ip rsvp bandwidth <max> <typical> sets bandwidth, ip rsvp reservation bandwidth per-flow sets per-flow caps, and ip rsvp neighbor defines explicit peers. Configure RSVP on every hop along the path.

cards.q: How do IntServ and DiffServ differ in unit, signaling, state, guarantee, and scale?
cards.a: IntServ works per-flow with RSVP signaling, holds per-flow state, gives hard guarantees, and scales poorly; DiffServ works per-class with no signaling, has per-class state, gives statistical guarantees, and scales well. DiffServ wins on scale; IntServ wins on guarantee.

cards.q: Where does IntServ live today and what is its surviving major use?
cards.a: It survives as RSVP-TE for MPLS traffic engineering, plus voice gateways on small segments and niche hard-guarantee uses. RSVP-TE (TE path setup) is the major surviving use.

cards.q: What command verifies RSVP reservations on an interface?
cards.a: show ip rsvp interface, show ip rsvp reservation, show ip rsvp sender, and show ip rsvp installed.

cards.q: A receiver is not getting a reservation; RESV is rejected. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: There is not enough RSVP bandwidth on a hop. Check show ip rsvp interface and the rsvp bandwidth configured on each router.

cards.q: What is the direction and job of PATH versus RESV in RSVP?
cards.a: PATH flows sender toward receiver to announce requirements; RESV flows receiver toward sender to reserve resources.

cards.q: Why does IntServ have poor scalability?
cards.a: Every router on the path must maintain per-flow reservation state, which does not scale to large networks, unlike DiffServ's per-class state.

cards.q: What is the modern surviving form of RSVP in MPLS networks?
cards.a: RSVP-TE, used for MPLS traffic engineering (TE path setup).
